Hi Daniel — great to hear from you and thanks for the clear list. I routed this to Ben (sales) and Marissa (security ops) to provide the detailed responses below; attaching our export spec and a small NDJSON sample so you can validate mapping.

Short answers first:
- Canonical schema: yes — our audit export contains the fields you listed plus event_type, user_agent, request_latency_ms, model_variant, kv_cache_hit, and redaction_reason where applicable. Exact field names are in the attached redwood_audit_export_spec_v1.pdf.
- Retention: hosted defaults to 90 days for request-level logs; Dedicated customers can configure retention down to 30 days or up to 7 years depending on contract; Private deployments support arbitrary retention policies (customer-managed).
- Export formats: we support NDJSON (recommended), compressed CSV (for small exports), and Parquet (analytics-ready). Exports can be full snapshots and incremental deltas (cursor-based) depending on your selection.
- Integrity: exports include SHA256 checksums for each file plus a signed manifest (we use AWS KMS for signing in hosted mode). For Dedicated/Private we can provide customer-supplied KMS integration.
- Delivery: presigned S3, SFTP push, or S3-to-S3 replication; standard lead time is 3 business days for on-demand exports, expedited options are available under enterprise SLAs.

Ben and Marissa — see Daniel's original message below and the attached examples. Can one of you provide the contractual retention matrix and an example manifest with signed checksum details?

Hi Daniel — following up with the contractual/sku-level view you asked for. Attaching a short matrix in the playbook but summarizing inline: 

- Hosted (SaaS): default 90 days retention for request-level logs, 365 days for coarse billing traces; retention extensions to 7 years available as a paid add-on with a 30-day notice. Exports are available as ad-hoc snapshots or scheduled exports; lead time 3 business days standard.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools): retention configurable per-tenant via console; SLA-backed retention guarantees (we can commit retention windows in the contract). Exports support incremental cursors; we provide server-side encryption with either Redwood-managed keys or customer-managed KMS.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full customer control; export tooling runs in your environment. We provide scripts and an export agent (s3-exporter) which can produce NDJSON/Parquet and create signed manifests locally.

We support legal hold: exports can be pinned and excluded from retention deletion while you ship an evidence bundle. Pricing and commitments vary by tier — happy to send a redlined quote tied to retention terms once you confirm target retention.

Hi Daniel — Marissa from Security Ops here. A few additional details and clarifications to address your integrity and mapping concerns: 

1) Field-level provenance: every audit event includes a 'producer' and 'producer_version' field so you can trace which runtime emitted the record (useful when multiple model variants or regions are in play).
2) Prompt/response redaction: PII can be redacted at export time. When redaction occurs we include redaction_reason and a redaction_mask token that indicates the original data class (e.g., EMAIL, SSN) without exposing PII.
3) Checksums and manifests: sample manifest format is attached (manifest includes per-file SHA256, total record count, timestamp, and signature). For Hosted exports we sign manifests with Redwood KMS; for Dedicated/Private we support HSM/KMS BYOK and can produce PKCS#7 signatures if required.
4) Immutable storage: we support S3 WORM (object lock) for export delivery buckets and can attach a tamper-evidence report showing object lock configuration and retention settings.

I've attached sample-ndjson-export.ndjson (sanitized) and s3-delivery-playbook.pdf that show the manifest and an example transfer sequence. If you want, we can run a test export for a 7‑day sample dataset to confirm schema mappings and integrity checks.
